land.text: 'Sargon II razed the city c. 720 BC' and annexed Hama as an Assyrian province

successors.note: The Sargon II page has 'Hama and the other insurgent cities were annexed again'; the Hamath page has the city recolonized 'with 6300 Assyrians'.

capitals.name: Hamath (Hama)
capitals.note: The page treats the city of Hama on the Orontes as the kingdom's centre. Zakkur's fortress of Hazrak (Tell Afis) lies in the north; coordinates are those of modern Hama.

correction.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Hamath (its Neo-Assyrian shape of -700 covers the area). The page gives no area and no boundary; the shape is a 60 km circle round Hama (about 11,000 km2) as the researcher's reading. The page says 'Aram-Damascus seems to have taken over some of Hamath's territory' (undated), which is not subtracted. The start year is the first attestation (Qarqar, 853), not a founding.

correction.text: Hamath with its northern province Luhuti, 'king of Hamath and Luhuti'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Luhuti was incorporated into Hamath around 796 BC. It formed the northern province of the kingdom.' Zakkur is 'king of Hamath and Luhuti'. Luhuti is placed as the Idlib governorate (about 5,300 km2) because Hazrak (Tell Afis) is the fortress where Zakkur was besieged; the page gives no boundary. Total about 16,000 km2; no infobox area to compare.

correction.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in 738 Tiglath-Pileser III set up the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra, and 'Hamath is listed among the cities again conquered by Assyrian troops' (Hamath page); the northern province is therefore taken out (Hatarikka read as Luhuti/Hadrach) and the core stays as a tributary until 720.

region.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

ledger.note: 853 BC (first attestation): Hamath stands on the Orontes. Shalmaneser III 'reached Hamath (Assyrian: Amat or Hamata) in 853 BC; this marks the beginning of Assyrian inscriptions' (Hamath page); at Qarqar Irhuleni of Hamath led 700 chariots, 700 horsemen and 10,000 soldiers. The page gives no founding date or founder, so the start is a bridging judgment; the kingdom is older (undated: 'the site appears to have been prosperous around 1500 BC').

region.text: Luhuti, 'the northern province of the kingdom' with Hazrak (Tell Afis), where Zakkur was besieged

ledger.note: c. 796 BC: Luhuti joins Hamath. 'Luhuti was incorporated into Hamath around 796 BC. It formed the northern province of the kingdom.' Zakkur is 'king of Hamath and Luhuti'. Where Luhuti lay is not on the page; the Idlib governorate is the reading from Zakkur's fortress at Tell Afis.

region.text: Luhuti, 'the northern province of the kingdom' with Hazrak (Tell Afis), where Zakkur was besieged

ledger.note: 738 BC: Assyria takes Luhuti. Tiglath-Pileser III's page: 'establishing the three new provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka, and Simirra' in 738; Hatarikka is Hadrach/Hazrak, Zakkur's fortress (name match, not stated on either page). The Hamath page adds 'In 743 BC, Tiglath-Pileser III took a number of towns in the territory of Hamath' (not located).

region.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

ledger.note: 738 BC: Hamath becomes an Assyrian tributary. 'In 738 BC, Hamath is listed among the cities again conquered by Assyrian troops'; the page does not use the word tribute, and Hamath keeps its king until 720.

region.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

ledger.note: c. 720 BC: Yahu-Bihdi's revolt ends the tributary state. 'Yahu-Bihdi of Hama in Syria assembled a coalition of minor states' (Arpad, Damascus, Sumur, Samaria) 'shortly after' Sargon's failure in Babylonia in 720; 'Sargon engaged Yahu-Bihdi and his coalition at Qarqar on the Orontes'.

region.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

ledger.note: c. 720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hamath. 'Hama and the other insurgent cities were annexed again'; the Hamath page: 'Sargon II razed the city c. 720 BC', 'removed its king to be flayed alive in Assyria' and recolonized it with 6,300 Assyrians.

region.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

ledger.note: c. 720 BC: the kingdom of Hamath ends under Sargon II. The Aramean displaced from Hamath formed part of the community 'in Egypt starting in 700 BCE' (Hamath page).

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory; 'Shalmaneser's opponents held on to their thrones after this battle'. Irhuleni of Hamath sent 700 chariots, 700 horsemen and 10,000 soldiers.
wars.note: Qarqar is identified with Tell Qarqur in Hama Governorate. Another Hamath page sentence has Irhuleni co-leading the coalition with Hadadezer of Aram-Damascus.

wars.name: Siege of Hazrak (Zakkur against the Aramean coalition)
wars.outcome: 'Zakkur survived the siege' at Tell Afis; the coalition was incited by Ben-Hadad III and led by the king of Bit Agusi.
wars.note: The page dates neither the siege nor the stele; the span runs from Ben-Hadad III's reign start (796 BCE, from the aram-damascus dossier) to Zakkur's c. 785 BC mention. Adad-nirari III later had Shamshi-ilu mediate a border dispute between Zakkur and Atarshumki I of Arpad (undated).

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's campaigns against Hamath

zones.text: Luhuti, 'the northern province of the kingdom' with Hazrak (Tell Afis), where Zakkur was besieged

wars.outcome: Towns of Hamath taken in 743; Hamath again conquered in 738; the province of Hatarikka created.
wars.note: The Hamath page gives 743 ('took a number of towns in the territory of Hamath') and 738; the Tiglath-Pileser III page gives the three new provinces of 738.

wars.name: Revolt of Yahu-Bihdi against Sargon II

zones.text: Hamath on the Orontes in west-central Syria: the city of Hama and its valley

wars.outcome: Sargon II defeats Yahu-Bihdi at Qarqar on the Orontes, razes Hamath and annexes it as a province.
wars.note: The Sargon II page names the king 'Yahu-Bihdi of Hama' and gives no year for Qarqar or the annexation; 720 is the page's year for Sargon's Babylonian failure that immediately preceded the campaign.

certainty.note: No Hamathite boundary is given; the Arpad border was a dispute settled by Assyria c. 785.

sources.title: Hamath
sources.note: Mostly the city; Qarqar 853 BC, Aram-Damascus took territory (undated), Tiglath-Pileser III 743 and 738, Sargon II c. 720 BC.

sources.title: Zakkur
sources.note: King of Hamath and Luhuti c. 785 BC; Luhuti incorporated c. 796 BC; the siege at Tell Afis; Irhuleni and Uratami before Zakkur.

sources.title: Sargon II
sources.note: Yahu-Bihdi of Hama's coalition and its defeat at Qarqar; Hama annexed; undated except the 720 anchor.

sources.title: Battle of Qarqar
sources.note: 853 BC; Irhuleni of Hamath in the coalition; Tell Qarqur in Hama Governorate.

sources.title: Tiglath-Pileser III
sources.note: 738 BC provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra; 740 Arpad provinces.

notes: Cliopatria has no Hamath. The Hamath page is the modern city's article; it gives no founding, no king list and no area, so the start (853) is the first attestation, not a founding, and the kingdom's earlier life (Toi/Tou at David's time, a Neo-Hittite phase) is not on any page opened. Where Luhuti lay and what Hatarikka corresponds to are my readings (Idlib governorate; Hatarikka = Hadrach/Hazrak), flagged in the keyframe and ledger notes. Aram-Damascus's takeover of Hamathite territory (undated, 'seems to have') is not drawn. The Sargon II page names Qarqar but dates neither battle nor annexation. A gap-filler should open the page on the Neo-Hittite king list (Toi, Uratami, Zakkur) or 'Kingdom of Hamath' if one exists (the URL Hamath_(kingdom) was not tried).
